To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a simple probabilistic framework for discriminative k-shot learning can outperform state-of-the-art approaches by a large margin; 2) the probabilistic model is well-calibrated and easily extensible; and 3) the framework can be used to learn from a large initial dataset to perform k-shot learning on a new dataset with a small number of examples per class, without the need for a large-scale dataset for the new domain.

we have introduced a probabilistic framework to perform k-shot learning, and that we have shown that even a simple model can outperform state-of-the-art methods on the standard k-shot learning benchmark.

a probabilistic model of the final layer weights in a neural network can be used as a prior to achieve state-of-the-art k-shot classification performance, and that it is also able to accurately model classification uncertainty, leading to a well-calibrated classifier.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: Given a set of classes (C) and a set of images (I), what is the probability that an image belongs to a class?
how to learn a classifier from a small number of examples and how to use the knowledge learned from a previous task.

the following questions: How can we leverage knowledge learned from a large scale classification task for a new classification task with only a few examples? How can we learn from only a few examples in a way that is both accurate and calibrated?

probabilistic models provide a simple, flexible, and powerful framework for k-shot learning.
probabilistic modelling can be an effective way to leverage the information in large-scale classification problems to solve k-shot learning tasks.
